answer: Charged entry inlet: each new agent identity must pay a non-refundable fee to a shared garden pool before its first transaction, and that fee is released only after 30 days of unique counterparties. An attacker cloning N identities pays N fees up front with delayed return, while honest agents amortize one fee. Sybils also risk umber-flagged limits: clones sharing behavioral fingerprints lose pool access, making each marginal clone a sunk cost.
